prob.title: Why most HYROX plans fail
p1.d: A fast 10 km says little. After burpees and sleds your legs are compromised — without specific work you lose 20–60 s per km in the second half.
p2.d: Most calculators only look at your running. Sleds, lunges and wall balls decide 35–45 % of your time — and that is exactly where most athletes have the biggest gains.
p3.d: Generic plans stack volume and impact without looking at how you recover. Achilles and calves pay the price in week 6.
sol.title: Six things Benchmrk does differently
s1.d: Your finish time = 8 runs + 8 stations + Roxzone, from your ratings, PRs and benchmark splits. You see where the minutes are.
s2.d: Heart-rate zones on your own threshold HR (Friel %LTHR), capped at your max HR. No fixed numbers from someone else.
s3.d: Threshold test, threshold endurance, compromised pacing, pace-decay test and a full dress rehearsal recalibrate your paces — corrected for heart rate.
s4.d: Log pace, HR and RPE. Twice too slow at high HR? Targets ease off. Stiff tendons in the morning? Impact days switch to low-impact.
s5.d: Team code, one shared prediction, a split per station from both partners' times and a shared sim day.
s6.d: Weekly station strength aimed at your two weakest stations, progressing towards your division's race weights.

sci.title: What the plan is built on
sci1: VO₂max, aerobic training volume and body-fat % correlate most with HYROX finish time; runs are roughly 60 % of the race for recreational athletes.
sci2: HYROX is mostly horizontal work — running, sleds and carries — and needs specific training rather than generic CrossFit-style sessions.
sci3: Heart-rate zones as a percentage of your own lactate-threshold heart rate.
sci4: Official station weights per division, from Open women to Pro men.

faq.title: Questions
q1: I don't know my threshold heart rate.
a1: Use your Garmin estimate, or run 30 minutes as hard as you can sustain alone: your average HR over the last 20 minutes is a good estimate. Benchmark 1 corrects it.
q2: Does it work for doubles with different levels?
a2: Yes. The slower runner sets the pace, stations are split on both partners' strengths and you both see the same team prediction.
a3: Only you see your data. In a doubles team your partner sees your sessions and benchmarks; nobody else does.

land.sub: A plan on your own threshold, from today to race day, built around compromised running: running on tired legs. Plan your whole season, with main races and stepping-stone races. With an honest finish-time prediction that includes your stations, and five benchmarks that recalibrate everything, solo or doubles.
land.f5d: Link your gym and follow its HYROX programme. Plan around WODs you don't control, or train at home with what you've got. Your plan works with the location and equipment of each day.
land.f6d: In research on recreational athletes, more than 60% of race time was spent running. Almost every kilometre starts on tired legs. That's why your plan centres on running after the stations.
tour.title: How your plan adapts
tour.sub: Five moments from a training season, from your weekly plan to an injury.
tour.note: Example, calculated live with the same engine as your plan. No real user data.
tour.s1.h: Your whole season in one plan
tour.s1.d: Enter your races and label each as a main race or a stepping-stone race. The plan counts back from every main race and fits the others in as hard training. Every day comes with a pace and a heart-rate cap.
tour.s2.d: Training at a gym or with a coach? Take a photo of the board. The app reads the WOD, recognises the stations and counts the load in your week.
tour.s2.load: At RPE 8 or higher it counts as a hard day, and the rest of your week takes that into account.
tour.s3.d: Log pace, heart rate and RPE. The app compares them with your zones and target. Twice too slow at a high heart rate? It suggests easing your paces a little.
tour.s4.d: Tell the app what's going on. Running becomes cross-training at the same heart rate, stations that load the injury drop out and you get a rehab block. After the return test you build back up over three weeks.
tour.s4.note: Always have an injury assessed by a physiotherapist or doctor.
tour.s5.d: Enter the gym code and your weekly sim follows your gym's build-up, with the equipment it has. Paces, heart rate and race date stay yours.
tour.s5.template: Your gym's sim build-up, per week
tour.s5.own: When the gym updates its template, your plan moves with it.
fit.title: Makes what you already do stronger
fit.sub: Benchmrk doesn't replace your gym, your coach or your races. It turns them into one plan.
fit.gym.d: With a gym code, members follow the gym's sim build-up and equipment. Everyone keeps their own plan on their own threshold and race date.
fit.pt.d: Log sessions with your coach as a WOD day, or scan the whiteboard. Your plan counts the load and fills in the rest of your week. Coaching a regular group? Then it works the same as a gym.
fit.race.d: Plan your season around the races in the official calendar. Pick your division per race, and the plan uses the official weights.
fit.watch.d: Keep your watch and your own apps. Benchmrk only asks for pace, heart rate and RPE, and shows where to find your threshold in Garmin, Apple, Polar or Coros.
